text.p: PRESS DIGEST - Romania - Aug 7
Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Romania imported over 3.5 tonnes of insecticides last year, three times more than in 1993, but the market is also invaded by huge amounts of unauthorised substances, says the newspaper.
- Romania's national press agency Rompres needs 2.6 billion lei to avoid going bankrupt, says Constantin Badea, manager of the agency.
- Rail transport would recover only if ticket prices were more than doubled, says the newspaper in a two-page report on the state of Romanian railways.
- The newspaper presents doctors' opinions on the new health insurance law, a key part of the reform of the health care system which reinstates the family doctor.
BURSA
- More than 66 perecnt of Romanians do not want to sell privatisation coupons, according to a survey.
ADEVARUL
- Under the revised 1997 budget, the Education Ministry will get 400 billion lei more, while the Agriculture Ministry loses 399 billion lei.
- Poul Thomsen, the IMF's chief negotiator for Romania, said unproductive companies must be closed.
- Foreign capital still avoids Romania as big companies are not rushing to invest, compared to the investors with "10 dollars in their pocket" who invade the country, says the newspaper.
- The central bank has drawn up regulations for repatriation of the foreign capital.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- To support small and midium-sized companies, next year regional fonds will be created to guarantee credits.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The government paid 112 billion lei to cover the debt of the national railway company to Romanian train wagon producer Astra Vagoane Arad.
- For seven years state-run companies produced only for output's sake, says the newspaper. Inventories accounted for almost 70 percent of the total industrial output in May.
- Romanian exports in the first five months are more than three billion dollars.
General
ADEVARUL

- The Alliance for Romania (APR), a new party built by dissidents from the former ruling Party of Social Democracy, proposes eliminating one of the parliament's two chambers. APR describes itself as "republican, national and anti-extremist".
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The newspaper presents a full-page report on how hundreds of Romanians wait night and day at Western embassies to obtain a visa. Romania is still on "the black list" of the European Union, its citizens having to apply for a visa to enter EU countries.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The cases against Razvan Temesan, former head of the leading state-run Bancorex bank and George Constantin Paunescu, Romania's most prominent businessman, are political trials, says the head of the Human Rights Defence League.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Following a government decision to place bilingual plaques of towns and villages, the Hungarian Democratic Union wants places in central Transylvania to revert to old names.

- Florin Cioaba, self-proclaimed king of Gyspies in Romania, will ask Germany for 350 million marks in damages for extermination of more than 10,000 Gypsies in the death camps of Auschwitz and Birkenau.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
